before.name: SaltyCloud
before.description: Isora GRC risk assessment, vendor review and compliance workflow software for higher education and public sector security teams - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Isora GRC is software that gives security teams one connected workspace to run assessments, manage vendors and assets, track risks, and prove compliance. It is positioned against spreadsheets and against enterprise GRC platforms that require months of setup, dedicated admins, and consultant-driven configuration. Questionnaires are structured and aligned to frameworks such as NIST, CIS, GLBA, and HECVAT, and contributors upload evidence inline and route responses for approval.

For third-party work, the platform connects vendor questionnaires, inventory records, risk findings, and reporting in one workspace. Vendor assessments cover HECVAT, SIG, and CAIQ, and a one-click HECVAT uploader imports completed spreadsheets, matches responses, and scores automatically. Findings flow into a collaborative risk register carrying lineage from questionnaire to control to risk, where owners are assigned and remediation is tracked.

The solutions index describes the product for public sector institutions, for financial institutions such as banks and credit unions, and for information security teams. Higher education institutions managing hundreds of vendors are described as using it as their primary vendor assessment platform.

before.name: ITO Health
before.description: Medicaid eligibility screening, benefits enrollment and social needs care management software for government agencies, FQHCs and payers - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: ITO Health is a Public Benefit Company built by clinicians and health professionals. It makes tools that help care workers and benefits specialists connect people to the support they need. The customers are health and social care organizations running the workflows behind eligibility decisions, enrollment, and ongoing coordination.

HealthBase and HealthWorks are the core offerings, sibling configurations of the same platform for different operational needs. HealthBase turns client information into completed benefit applications and real-world actions rather than referrals. HealthWorks is the employer-facing version, a benefit navigation platform for workforces. Eligibility decision support applies deterministic logic across more than 120 federal, state, and local programs to produce auditable determinations.

HealthBase is built for social service organizations, federally qualified health centers, community health centers, and healthcare systems that coordinate benefits enrollment and social care. The products page puts current eligibility and enrollment coverage at more than 75 federal and local programs. The platform supports HL7 FHIR, custom API integrations, and connections to electronic health records. The company states that it is a HIPAA-compliant organization. It says clinicians founded it.

before.name: Intrado Life & Safety
before.description: 911 call routing, Viper call handling and NG911 for PSAPs

paragraphs: Intrado sells call handling and management systems for emergency response. It describes itself as the connective tissue that gets the right help to the right location as quickly as possible.

Alongside the call center products, one line keeps employees safe wherever they work while meeting state and federal regulations. Another covers incident management for schools from prevention through response and recovery. For carriers, call routing, location and data products connect subscribers to emergency services and keep providers compliant. Network services are offered to improve call routing and data sharing and to deliver on i3 compliance. ECaTS, the Emergency Call Tracking System, generates descriptive reports from 9-1-1 call data.

The company puts its history in the emergency services industry at 45 years. That history includes acquisitions of Lucent Public Safety, Positron Public Safety Systems, ECaTS, 911 ETC and 911 Enable. Headquarters are in Longmont, Colorado, with a manufacturing site in Montreal, Quebec. The company reports approximately 950 employees worldwide, most of them in the Longmont and Montreal regions.

before.description: Public-sector HR suite: recruiting, onboarding, and performance - exhibited at PSHRA 2026

paragraphs: NEOGOV sells human resources software for government agencies, built around public sector hiring, onboarding, and compliance. The platform is described as purpose-built for government agencies, municipalities, and the broader public sector, with forms, workflows, and reporting aligned to public sector regulations. Products named on the site include Insight for applicant tracking, Attract for candidate relationship management, and Onboard for employee onboarding.

Insight is presented as an applicant tracking system that automates and centralizes recruitment activities for public sector hiring. Insight supports civil service requirements such as minimum qualifications screening, canvassing letters, and ranked eligibility lists, according to that page. Attract is a candidate relationship management system for agencies to engage candidates who have expressed interest in government jobs.

GovernmentJobs.com is offered as a job board built for public sector recruitment, with jobs posted in Insight published there automatically. The site also lists onboarding, performance management, learning management, custom forms, background investigations, and compliance management among the functions covered.

before.name: Aurigo Software
before.description: Masterworks capital program and construction management for DOTs, cities, water, and transit

paragraphs: Aurigo Software sells capital program management software to government agencies that plan, build and maintain public infrastructure. It also serves facility owners in areas such as data centers, life sciences, manufacturing, and energy and utilities. The company's platform, Masterworks, brings planning, execution, financials, right of way and analytics together in one system.

On the delivery side it coordinates contracts, schedules, costs and field work so teams can hold to the original plan and keep a complete audit trail. Compliance, funding transparency and governance are meant to sit inside everyday work so public money stays accountable. Agencies can change forms, workflows, business rules and dashboards through configuration rather than code. An AI layer called Lumina supports decision-making with compliance and governance built in, and the company says every insight and recommendation it produces can be audited and traced.

Cities, counties, transit agencies and transportation departments across North America use the platform to manage capital programs, replace legacy systems and automate federal reimbursements. The company claims more than 300 customers and over 20 years of capital program expertise behind the product. It also says the software monitors project signals to catch cost, schedule and delivery risks before they turn critical.

before.name: Carbyne
before.description: Cloud-native 911 call handling with live video, location, and AI triage

paragraphs: Carbyne builds and supports Axon 911 Core, a cloud-native infrastructure layer deployed in agencies across the United States and internationally. Its call-handling product, APEX, pulls call management capabilities into a single user interface for telecommunicators.

Patented live video lets responders see through the eyes of a caller. Location tools pinpoint a caller and track movement as permitted. AI-powered translation arrives directly on the call taker's screen. During call surges, an AI triage tool sorts through calls to identify redundant bystander and onlooker reports, freeing call takers for other emergencies. A continuity option has the AT&T Resolution Center redirect 911 calls and texts to devices running APEX Continuity. That reroute is triggered manually by the center rather than automatically.

The company states 99.999% call-handling uptime in the cloud. It describes the platform as providing the security of AWS GovCloud. Carbyne counts more than 100 partners and over 40 integrations on its open platform. The site names Orleans Parish Communication District as a center using its Emergency Call Triage.

before.name: Miovision
before.description: Traffic data collection and smart intersection technology

paragraphs: Miovision sells traffic data collection tools meant to give planners the accurate, verifiable data their mobility plans depend on. It also sells detection equipment that improves signal performance by responding to real-world road user demand, from bicycles to articulated trucks. Its Opticom line clears the path for emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.

Portable devices capture comprehensive multimodal count data including cars, trucks, pedestrians and bikes. A newer optimization product replaces manual five-year retiming cycles with iterative, objective-based optimization that the company says cuts manual effort by up to half. Engineers compare plans side-by-side, validate against industry standards, and push updates directly to field controllers without manual data re-entry.

The company says that since 2005 it has had 2,000 customers in 68 countries and 13,000 cities, with 30 billion vehicles and 1.5 billion pedestrians counted. It lists more than 300 detection customers in North America. Detroit partnered with Miovision to upgrade over 600 intersections. In San Rafael, police and fire vehicles now receive signal priority at 53 intersections.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© AT&T Intellectual Property. All rights reserved. FirstNet and the FirstNet logo are registered trademarks and service marks of the First Responder Network Authority." Fetched https://www.firstnet.com. The entity question in the CAUTION resolves cleanly: the footer copyright is AT&T's ('© AT&T Intellectual Property'), while the FirstNet marks are acknowledged as belonging to the First Responder Network Authority — i.e. this domain is the AT&T-operated commercial service, which is exactly the board entity 'FirstNet, Built with AT&T'. I confirmed the split by also fetching the federal side: firstnetauthority.gov states 'The First Responder Network Authority is an independent agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration' and sends users elsewhere for service with 'Access my FirstNet account (FirstNet.com).' So .gov is the agency, .com is the AT&T service. On rule 3: firstnet.com is NOT the parent's corporate domain (that is att.com) — it is the product's own dedicated domain with its own branding, plans and support, so it is acceptable. FLAG for the board operator, though: FirstNet does not recruit as a separate employer. Sales roles on this product are posted as AT&T requisitions, so a scraper pointed at firstnet.com will like

paragraphs: Recollect sells a cloud-based Collection Management System for galleries, libraries, archives, museums, academic institutions and heritage sites. The product is presented as management and discovery for a digital collection, held in a single digital repository built to support staff, students, and researchers. Metadata and contextual information configure the site and link assets together, and content of any format is reached from any device.

The about page lists the organisations the platform supports, beginning with libraries, archives and museums wanting to digitise and share their collections. That list also names local government bodies preserving public records. It further names indigenous and marginalised communities seeking tools for managing culturally sensitive materials, and educational institutions providing students and researchers with accessible resources.

The same page states that by 2020 the company became a standalone entity, expanding into the USA, UK, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong. It reports support for over 160 sites globally. Case studies name the Museum of Flight, Palos Verdes Library District, the State Library of Oregon and Denver Public Library.

paragraphs: Ad Astra sells scheduling and academic planning software to colleges and universities. One platform covers course scheduling and campus event management for higher education institutions.

Schedulers build sections on a visual grid, handling buildings, spaces, faculty and room assignments in the same workflow. Recommendations drawn from historical enrollment patterns point to changes that ease course bottlenecks. Finished schedules and later edits publish straight to the campus student information system. paragraphs: Gainwell sells the systems that run state Medicaid programs, tying together claims and encounter management, provider contracts, capitation and member benefits. Pharmacy is a separate line aimed at medication management and the total cost of care. Another line helps payers avoid and recover improper payments while detecting fraud.

The claims, encounters and financials module is presented as a modernization step built on automation and interoperability. An EDI gateway lets providers submit all their claims centrally, which the company says simplifies Medicaid billing. Its analytics platform is shaped around Medicaid data and federal compliance requirements. Provider management can be modernized in phases with Provider Flex, replaced outright with Provider+, or extended across state lines through a cross-state provider network.

The analytics page cites 52 state Medicaid programs. A case study on the home page covers provider enrollment in Vermont. That case study claims an 87.5% reduction in enrollment processing time. Its centralized credentialing platform is described as NCQA accredited. The company points to longstanding experience keeping Medicaid programs running with accurate data for decision making.

before.name: Electro Scan
before.description: Machine-based pipe defect and leak assessment for municipal sewer and water - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Electro Scan sells leak detection and lead pipe location work for water and sewer systems. The company says municipal sewer utilities and sewer contractors use it to pin down the location, measurement and flow of defects inside a pipe before a repair or replacement job.

The method rests on a simple claim: pipe defects that leak water also leak electricity, so a defect shows up whether or not it happens to be leaking during the inspection. A low voltage conductivity probe travels through the pipe at 45 to 60 feet per minute, locating and measuring defects as it goes. Crews can then create summary and detail level reports for a team to review. The flagship probe is built for gravity mains between 6 and 30 inches in diameter, and the company says agencies and contractors use it worldwide.

Electro Scan lists ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management systems. Its case studies page includes a North American benchmark study comparing closed-circuit television inspection with focused electrode leak location on gravity sewer mains. Other write-ups describe a Florida utility dealing with excessive inflow and infiltration in its gravity collection system.

before.name: FUNDVIEW
before.description: Fund accounting and ERP software for cities and local governments, covering financials, payroll, utility billing and municipal court - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: FUNDVIEW sells an ERP platform to local governments, covering finance, workforce, utilities, community development, and court and citizen services. The pitch is aimed at cities running several disconnected systems and entering the same figures by hand in each one.

Every module posts into the same real-time general ledger, which is what removes the second entry. The finance side covers budgets, purchasing, payables, reconciliation, assets, cash receipting and reporting. Workforce management joins payroll, human resources and employee time onto one record. Court receipts reach finance as they are taken rather than at month end.

The company says more than 180 Texas local governments run on the platform. It states that fund accounting, financial statements and audit documentation follow GASB and GAAP standards. Payroll reporting covers 941, TMRS, TWC, E-Verify, new hire and year-end wage filings.

before.name: Maximus
before.description: Eligibility, enrollment and program administration for state HHS agencies - exhibited at GFOA 2026, NCSEA 2026

paragraphs: Maximus sells technology and program operations to government agencies working in health, human services, veteran support, citizen experience, defense, and national security. Homepage headings group the work as technology services, customer experience, health and clinical services, and program delivery. Named offerings include omnichannel contact center solutions for federal and state agencies, tools to reduce SNAP error rates and case backlogs, and veteran services delivered through AI and digital transformation.

The case studies page lists state work, including a SNAP surge in Wisconsin and SNAP replacement benefits delivered in Texas after natural disasters. Another case study says the Texas Health and Human Services Commission contracted Maximus to integrate eligibility support services for TANF, SNAP, Medicaid, and CHIP. Other entries describe centralized credentialing for Medicaid provider networks in Ohio and a transition from the federal exchange to a state-based marketplace for Maine.

Federal examples on the same page include an AI-Powered Medical Records Processing System for disability benefits applications at the VA. The page also credits Maximus with supporting the modernization of HRSA’s Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network. Another entry says automation helped CMS streamline No Surprises Act case processing.

before.description: Modular ACA marketplace, Medicaid eligibility verification and AI platforms for state and federal health and human services agencies - exhibited at APHSA 2026, NAMPI 2026

paragraphs: CITIZ3N Government Solutions builds modular platforms for government agencies that oversee Affordable Care Act marketplaces, Medicaid, health and human services programs, and health benefits for government employees. It is a subsidiary of Softheon and one of three brands in that portfolio.

There are two platforms: MARKETPLACE, a set of stand-alone modules meant to integrate into marketplace exchanges for government, and VERIFY, which handles eligibility determinations and combats fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid and HHS programs. Both are delivered as cloud-based software as a service. The architecture is cloud-native and uses an enterprise service bus for communication and interoperability between systems. The company says the platforms scale to more than a million transactions per day.

The buyers are local, state, and federal agencies. The company states compliance with HIPAA and regular security audits against frameworks such as NIST 800-53 and MARS-E 2.0. Its annual audits are listed as SOC 1 and 2, PCI AOC, a NACHA audit, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and code security scanning. Support is described as implementation assistance, training programs, and ongoing technical help.

quote.text: Our goal and vision is to make healthcare affordable, accessible, and plentiful for all Americans.

before.name: Envisio
before.description: Strategic planning, performance measurement, and public dashboards built for local government

paragraphs: Envisio makes software for public agencies that need to turn a strategic plan into tracked work and reportable results. It is built for the public sector and, the company says, only the public sector. Customers span government, education, healthcare and nonprofit organizations.

Plans can be laid out as a cascade, a Gantt chart, tags or scorecards, depending on how the organization works. Staff get scheduled reminders to submit progress and performance updates. Those updates roll up automatically into reports covering actions, projects, measures and narrative. The same material feeds public dashboards a community can read. Every package includes unlimited users.

More than 200 organizations use Envisio, by the company's count. Example dashboards on the site include the City of Rockville's climate action plan, which tracks emissions reduction and renewable energy adoption. The company frames its purpose around a stated decline in trust in public institutions. It points to recognition as a GovTech 100 company. Chief executive Craig Ross was previously interim CEO at Euna Solutions and CEO of eCivis.

quote.text: Too often, those plans get stuck in spreadsheets, and nothing changes.

before.name: Mission Driven Data
before.description: Janet data platform that replicates and reports on Credible EHR data for behavioral health agencies - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: Mission Driven Data sells Janet, a tool that automates replication of a Credible database into a standard SQL database format, updated every night or on demand. Hundreds of agencies use the Credible EHR to record information about services, schedule appointments, process billing and financial transactions, and e-prescribe. Janet adds a wraparound layer over that system, with reporting and analytics on Microsoft Power BI dashboards, data integration and warehousing, notifications and workflow optimization.

The agencies addressed on the homepage offer a wide range of mental health and social services, some supporting rural areas with a staff of a few dozen and others serving thousands of clients a year. Janet also delivers the WHO-5 Well-Being Index to agency clients weekly by automatic text message, connecting that survey data to the agency Credible data. The about page states that leaders at over 50 behavioral health agencies and organizations nationwide rely on Janet.

before.name: Tantalus Systems
before.description: Smart grid AMI and grid analytics for public power utilities and co-ops

paragraphs: Tantalus is a technology company selling grid modernization systems to public power and electric cooperative utilities. It has been delivering data-centric products to that market for more than 35 years.

The products sit on the Tantalus Grid Modernization Platform, a modular architecture meant to move data across devices, systems and vendors. One piece is edge-computing metering infrastructure aimed at resiliency, reliability and lower total cost of ownership. Another handles load management and distributed energy resources sitting behind the meter. A gateway device fits any ANSI meter socket and adds visibility and control behind the meter without replacing the meter itself.

Utilities across North America partner with the company on distribution grid work, with published case studies including one in Bolivar, Tennessee. Tantalus Systems trades on the TSX under the symbol GRID and on OTCQX. It is based in Burnaby, British Columbia. Recent announcements include a debt restructuring and an annual survey of how utilities view grid modernization.

before.name: SmartCover Systems
before.description: Remote sewer level and overflow monitoring for municipal collection systems

paragraphs: SmartCover sells remote monitoring and controls for sewer, lift stations and stormwater infrastructure. The company describes the offering as turning real-time remote infrastructure data into insights for utility customers who want to minimize OpEx and reduce CapEx. Stated uses include overflow prevention, cleaning schedules, I&I identification, and chemical optimization.

The pages present satellite communication as what keeps the system visible. Alarms and notifications are described as giving advance notice so staff can prepare and respond. Installation is described as needing no confined space entry, with the work done in shop. A mobile app is offered, with system insights available wherever the user is.

A published case study covers the City of Kelowna in British Columbia. That city is described as using the technology for overflow prevention, optimization of high frequency cleaning, and ongoing I&I studies. Other departments in the city are described as using it for H2S monitoring, leachate at the solid waste facility, and stream level monitoring.

quote.text: Uninterrupted visibility of the system reduces risks, avoids damages and fees, and encourages efficiencies.

provenance.quote: Our remote monitoring and controls for sewer, lift stations and stormwater infrastructure enable utilities to eliminate overflows
SmartCover® transforms real-time remote infrastructure data into insights helping utility customers minimize OpEx, reduce CapEx and improve environmental performance.
Information drives overflow prevention, cleaning schedules, I&I identification, and chemical optimization.
Satellite Communication Delivers Constant System Visibility
Alarms and notifications provide advanced notice to prepare and respond.
No confined space entry and in-shop installation limit field resources and safety hazards.
Gain system insights wherever you are, whenever you need it.
The City of Kelowna is leveraging many of SmartCover’s unique features, including the off grid aspect of satellite communications
overflow prevention, optimization of high frequency cleaning, and ongoing I&I studies
In addition, other departments in the city were able to take advantage of SmartCover technology for H2S monitoring, leachate at the solid waste facility, and stream level monitoring.

before.name: Regroup Mass Notification
before.description: Emergency and routine mass notification for cities, counties and schools

paragraphs: Regroup sells a mass notification platform that organizations use for emergency alerts and for everyday operational messages in one place. Government buyers use it to reach residents quickly and to improve communication among their own staff.

Alerts go out by text message, email, voice call, and social media. Messages can be aimed at a specific area through geofencing. Recipients can reply, so senders learn who is safe and who needs help. The platform also connects to federal and regional public warning systems. For larger incidents, a dashboard gives one interface for monitoring every part of an event as it unfolds.

Regroup dates its service to 2006. The company says onboarding, unlimited training, and around the clock support come at no extra cost. Comments published on the site come from county emergency management offices, among other customers. Schools and campuses are another audience, with alerts for lockdowns and similar emergencies.

quote.text: Keep Your Organization Safe, Connected, and Running

provenance.quote: Regroup’s mass notification platform unifies emergency communication and daily operations in one simple system.
Reliably deliver critical updates to citizens quickly & improve internal communication.
Send alerts via SMS, email, voice calls, and social media.
Send location-based alerts using Geofence Messaging.
Allow recipients to respond and provide updates.
Comply with federal and regional public warning systems.
This feature provides a unified interface to manage and monitor all aspects of a critical event
Service You Can Trust Since 2006
Regroup includes a dedicated onboarding team, unlimited training, and ongoing 24x7 customer support from real humans at no extra cost.
Emergency Management Deputy Director - Comanche County
Alert students and staff during school lockdowns, active shooter situations, or other emergencies.

paragraphs: D-Fend Solutions sells counter-drone systems to military, law enforcement and homeland security agencies. Its core product, EnforceAir, detects a rogue drone, takes control of it through a radio-frequency cyber takeover and brings it to a safe landing. The company describes the approach as non-kinetic and AI-enhanced, built for sensitive and challenging environments.

EnforceAir can operate autonomously or under manual control, and it detects, locates and identifies rogue drones in a protected airspace before taking them over. It is sold in several deployment packages, including a Homeland Security & Law Enforcement Bundle and two tactical configurations, EnforceAir PLUS and EnforceAir2. EnforceAir PLUS, launched in August 2025, adds radar and a jammer to the RF-cyber layer. Beyond agencies, the company says the system has been chosen for large-scale events at stadiums, arenas and open-air venues and for VIP protection.

In an August 2026 press release the company says EnforceAir provided counter-drone security across World Cup host cities and was adopted by more than 20 public safety agencies. Chairman and CEO Zohar Halachmi co-founded the company after founding two mobile and enterprise application start-ups. Its U.S. arm, D-Fend Solutions AD, Inc., is located in McLean, Virginia. In June 2026 the company announced an agreement to be acquired by Motorola Solutions. Its newsroom now states that it has officially joined Motorola Solutions.

quote.text: To truly take full control of a dangerous drone situation, the key is taking control of the drone itself, and staying in control throughout the incident.

paragraphs: Transoft Solutions makes software for the people who plan, design and operate transportation systems. Its work spans aviation, civil infrastructure, transportation and operational professionals. On the aviation side that means specialized software to plan, analyze and optimize airport and airspace operations.

The company started in 1991, when co-founder Milton Carrasco developed a vehicle tracking program called AutoTURN. That product grew out of his master's thesis on computerized vehicle-turning simulation. The range has widened since through in-house development and strategic acquisitions. One executive is credited with merging AeroTURN and PathPlanner into AviPLAN.

The company reports more than 100,000 customers in over 150 countries. Clients are described as government agencies at the federal, state, county and municipal levels, along with major international airports and engineering and architectural design firms. Headquarters are in British Columbia, Canada, with further offices in the United States, Australia, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Germany, France, Sweden, Spain, India and China.

paragraphs: Kova Corp sells communication, recording and alerting software for public safety organizations and for enterprises. The products page splits the catalogue into public safety solutions, enterprise workforce optimization solutions and an emergency alerting solution.

KEANS, the KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System, links multiple locations, agencies, business partners and public address systems such as loudspeakers, bull horns and audio distribution repeaters. KAMS, the Kova Alarm Monitoring Solution, handles hardware monitoring, captures SNMP alerts and OS events, and can monitor data streams such as CDR, P25 traffic and RTP.

The workforce optimization page offers contact centers a platform for multimedia recording, evaluation and archiving of calls, plus an Enterprise Feedback Management survey platform and a Workforce Management solution. The about page names 911 call centers and emergency responders as the people those public safety solutions serve. The about page also cites a recorder installed for the Port Authority of NY/NJ after the loss of its Emergency Operations Center.

quote.text: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

provenance.quote: Kova Corp delivers reliable solutions for enterprise and security intelligence and alerting, efforts supported by our partnerships with global leaders in public safety.

Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

KEANS (KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System) provides reliable, simultaneous communication between multiple locations, agencies, business partners, and public address systems (such as loudspeakers, bull horns, and audio distribution repeaters).

KAMS provides not only the typical Hardware monitoring (CPU usage, memory, drive space, temperature, etc.) along with capturing SNMP alerts and OS events, but also can monitor critical data streams like CDR, P25 traffic, and RTP.
Kova recording solutions for contact centers provide a high performance platform for the multimedia recording, evaluation, and archiving of calls.

Our public safety solutions enable 911 call centers to function more efficiently, allow emergency responders to instantly share vital information, and make it possible to record and decipher data gathered.
KOVA offered immediate assistance to the Port Authority of NY/NJ, when it lost its Emergency Operations Center on 9/11. Within twenty-four hours, KOVA installed a new recorder at a temporary site.

paragraphs: Reunitus sells lost and found management and baggage resolution through software and managed service offerings. The offering is grouped into baggage resolution, lost item resolution, and unclaimed item monetization. Items that cannot be reunited are resold, and the company says it pays upfront based on full retail value.

NetTracer is a web-based tracing and resolution system that gained broad market adoption in North America. BagCentral launched as a baggage managed service for the airline industry, handling outsourced tasks such as baggage resolution and claims processing. Virtual services vBSO and vBagAgent were created to support airline partners.

Named partners include airlines, casinos, public venues, resorts, car rental providers, theme parks, cruise lines, and ground transportation companies. Airports and ground transportation also appear under the heading for who the company serves. The about page describes that work as streamlining lost item tracing, management, and resolution for airlines, airports, casinos, resorts, and theme parks.

paragraphs: Frequentis supplies communication and information systems for control centres with safety-critical tasks. The work splits between air traffic management, civil and military, and public safety and transport.

On the public safety side the buyers are police, fire brigades, ambulance services, coastguards and port authorities. Voice communication for air traffic control is the anchor, and the company puts its share of that market at around 30%. It also sells aeronautical information management and aeronautical message handling systems. Current development centres on digital remote tower technology, drone management and 5G/LTE in safety-critical applications.

The Austrian company is headquartered in Vienna and was founded in 1947. It keeps a network of branches, subsidiaries and local representatives in more than 50 countries. Around 550 customers in approximately 150 countries rely on its know-how, by its own count. Installed operator positions number around 49,000 worldwide. More than 75% of employees come from science, technology, engineering and mathematics backgrounds.

before.name: Tadera
before.description: Airport management software suite spanning lease/billing revenue management, Part 139 operations and safety compliance, gate management and secure credentialing.

paragraphs: Tadera sells airport software, and its staff includes former airport leaders along with subject matter experts in security, accounting, safety, and human resources. The finance tools are aimed at airports and systems of airports, covering property management, contracts, lease terms, billing, receivable and reporting, as well as capital improvement programs. A separate Secure Credentials product handles biometric credentialing, badging, continuous vetting, auditing, and access management, and helps meet TSA security directives.

ABRM, the Airport Business and Revenue Manager, consolidates lease management, billing, revenue tracking, tenant communications, and financial reporting into one system, covering both aeronautical and non-aeronautical revenue streams. It supports lease terms including minimum annual guarantees, fixed rent escalations, CPIs, ceilings, and floors, and tracks lease data elements for GASB 87 compliance.

Airport Project Manager covers capital programs, with an AIP Management Module tracking applications, funding, and compliance for FAA, FEMA, and state and local grants. Airport System Manager is built for state departments of transportation, combining grant tracking, facility inspections, aircraft registration, licensing, project funding, and data analysis into one application.

paragraphs: Jacobs is a global professional services company that delivers consulting and advisory, design and implementation work across infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, environmental and technology challenges. The sectors listed on these pages include transport across airports, rail, roads and maritime, water, buildings, power transmission and distribution, and land use planning. Building solutions cover the planning, design, delivery and operation of buildings, from strategy and planning through design, delivery, operations and reinvestment.

A digital and AI line combines artificial intelligence, digital advisory and enterprise software for organizations that plan, build and operate infrastructure. Intelligent O&M applies AI-driven analytics to wastewater and drinking water treatment plants, predicting failures and optimizing processes. StreetLight applies location-based analytics to show how people and goods move, for planning and operating decisions across transportation networks.

Clients named on these pages include the Central Utah Water Conservancy District, which selected Jacobs for engineering services on the proposed Strawberry High Line Improvement Project. The Orange County Transportation Authority selected Jacobs for construction management on two highway improvement projects in Orange County, California. Tilt Renewables selected Jacobs as owner's engineer for the Palmer Wind Farm near Adelaide, South Australia.

paragraphs: Gatekeeper Systems sells video recording and data systems for transportation, meant to make travel safer for children, passengers, and public safety personnel across several modes. The company says it uses AI, video analytics, thermal cameras, and mobile data collectors to inter-connect public transit assets within intelligent transportation systems.

Its mobile data collectors gather video and audio along with GPS tracking and door open and close events, analyzing the data on the bus itself. Those units are ruggedized and crashworthy, serving as black boxes that hold data for accident investigations. Recorders take analog and IP channels at up to 1080P and 30 frames per second, with independently selectable resolutions. Drive caddies have passed MIL SPEC 810F for shock and vibration, and a thermal system warms the hard drive to its prescribed operating temperature before writing or reading in cold weather.

Fleet software called G4 Vision centralizes system health checks, driver behavior analysis, video management, live streaming, GPS, routing and mapping, and student tracking. An Automated Lane Enforcement product for transit buses is named on the home page. The company describes a Platform-as-a-Service business model. Testimonials on that page are attributed to school district transportation directors.

before.name: AirBadge
before.description: Cloud identity management system (IDMS) purpose-built for US airport badge offices: applications, renewals, TSA audit compliance, training and scheduling, integrated with fingerprint, PACS (LenelS2) and training platforms.

paragraphs: AirBadge sells identity management software to airports in the United States, aimed at the badge office that issues and renews credentials. The company says it puts all of its resources into aviation so the software fits airport operations and TSA regulations. The product is described as built for 1542 and part 139 airports.

Applicants and badge holders enter their own details into the system. Those details are then sent directly to integrated systems, which removes a round of rekeying. It automates badge applications, appointment scheduling, training and testing, and cuts manual entry at fingerprinting, physical access control and TSC. Authorized signatories use it to invite new hires to apply and to authorize or block renewals. It runs on fully managed cloud infrastructure.

The site says more than 50 airports in the United States use it. It presents itself as a fit for airports of any size. The company announced LenelS2 factory certification and membership in the LenelS2 OpenAccess Alliance Program. Its software interfaces with the LenelS2 OnGuard access control system. Deployment is pitched in weeks rather than years.

paragraphs: SITA sells airport passenger processing software that moves a traveler from check-in through to boarding on common-use systems. The range covers Smart Path for identity management, Smart Path Kiosks, Smart Path Bag Drop and Smart Path Gates used for self-boarding, lounge access, security and border control. Flex Essentials is a common-use option for small and regional airports, and Flex as a Service is an API-based module for airlines.

A second group of products handles operations at airports, including flight information display, airport management and passenger information. Baggage products include Bag Journey for locating a bag, Bag Manager for reconciliation and WorldTracer for tracing mishandled bags.

These pages name airlines, airports and ground handlers as the users of the baggage and passenger products, and list governments among the industries served. Customer stories on the same page name Philadelphia International Airport, Geneva Airport and Shymkent International Airport.

paragraphs: RideCo sells on-demand transit software that agencies use to plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing transit costs. The software covers paratransit and microtransit, and the company attributes it to patented technology.

Products listed on the site include the Passenger App, the Driver App, Operations Center, Data Insights, Profile Manager, and Flex Fleets. The Passenger App lets riders request on-demand trips, preschedule them, or book recurring rides, and it is available on smartphones and on a standard web browser. Operations Center is a dashboard suite for streamlining operations and service monitoring in a transit dispatch center, with standardized and custom reports inside it.

Customers named on the site include MTA New York City Transit, which awarded a contract for its Access-A-Ride paratransit service. Other agencies named include the Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada and Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority, both for paratransit service.

quote.text: Together with RideCo, transit agencies can transform mobility for today and tomorrow.

provenance.quote: Our software is designed to help you plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing your transit costs.
With patented technology, RideCo’s on-demand paratransit and microtransit software is changing the way agencies deliver mobility to their communities.
In-vehicle driver facing application for automated vehicle location, mobile data communication, and real-time dispatch and data collection.
Using the Passenger App, riders can request on-demand trips or preschedule them in advance, book recurring rides, or schedule multiple trips at a time.
Reporting within Operations Center provides user-driven access to both standardized and custom reports.

paragraphs: Gatekeeper Systems sells video recording and data systems for transportation, meant to make travel safer for children, passengers, and public safety personnel across several modes. The company says it uses AI, video analytics, thermal cameras, and mobile data collectors to inter-connect public transit assets within intelligent transportation systems.

Its mobile data collectors gather video and audio along with GPS tracking and door open and close events, analyzing the data on the bus itself. Those units are ruggedized and crashworthy, serving as black boxes that hold data for accident investigations. Recorders take analog and IP channels at up to 1080P and 30 frames per second, with independently selectable resolutions. Drive caddies have passed MIL SPEC 810F for shock and vibration, and a thermal system warms the hard drive to its prescribed operating temperature before writing or reading in cold weather.

Fleet software called G4 Vision centralizes system health checks, driver behavior analysis, video management, live streaming, GPS, routing and mapping, and student tracking. An Automated Lane Enforcement product for transit buses is named on the home page. The company describes a Platform-as-a-Service business model. Testimonials on that page are attributed to school district transportation directors.

paragraphs: GIRO makes software for the organizations that run public transport and postal delivery services, covering the work from planning through daily operations. Its two product families, HASTUS and GeoRoute, are in use in more than 30 countries.

The company grounds the work in knowledge of the problems those operators face day to day. GIRO states that more than 30% of its resources go to research and development. New ideas and solutions are developed with clients and validated by groups of users around the world.

GIRO was founded in the 1970s through the work of a Université de Montréal student and his professor. That early work paved the way for the creation of both products. The company counts over 40 years of experience in the field. It also notes a ranking among the 300 largest companies in Quebec.

paragraphs: March Networks sells video surveillance systems for multi-site organizations, built from IP cameras, recorders, encoders and other hardware sold as one portfolio. Command Enterprise Software is the management layer for deploying and maintaining those video surveillance resources across a customer site. Searchlight, sold on premise or as a cloud service, turns the recorded video into loss prevention and business intelligence reporting.

The analytics catalogue covers people counting, heatmaps, dwell time, license plate recognition, and alerts for loitering, intrusion and blocked emergency exits. Detection runs on the AI Series cameras and on X-Series recorders built with NVIDIA system-on-chip technology, with alerts sent as mobile push notifications.

The company dates its founding to 2000 and puts retail, banking and transportation at the front of the industries it serves. The homepage counts more than 1,730 financial institutions, over 675 retailers and more than 735 commercial and industrial customers in over 75 countries. March Networks and VIVOTEK have merged their branded video security businesses, and the merged portfolio is presented across cloud, hybrid and on premise environments.

paragraphs: Interloc Solutions sells consulting and software for IBM Maximo, and the company describes a complete focus on Maximo across its services. Interloc also sells Mobile Informer, its own native app platform for Maximo mobility. A hosting service the pages call Maximo in the Cloud is offered alongside it. The consulting covers Maximo industry solutions and add-ons, among them Maximo Spatial Asset Management, Maximo Linear Asset Management, and the Maximo ERP Adapter.

Mobile Informer Work Management, shortened to iWM, runs on native applications and gives maintenance workers work orders, labor hours, meter readings and failure records on a device, online or offline. Mobile Informer Inventory Management, shortened to iIM, covers storeroom tasks such as issue, return, transfer, receipt and cycle count, and works with barcode readers and printers.

Testimonials on the home page are credited to Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART), to AUA Airport, and to Morgan Foods. The New York City Housing Authority is quoted on the work management page about staff recording data on mobile devices.

paragraphs: AngelTrax sells mobile video surveillance systems built for transportation safety. The company describes its customers as student transportation, mass transit, fleet, locomotive, and waste operations.

On a school bus, interior, exterior, stop-arm, and windshield views cover students, drivers, and transportation staff. Footage leaves the vehicle two ways, and a cellular link carries live view, active tracking, and instant notifications. Wi-Fi handles automated downloads once vehicles return to range. Video and data can be hosted by AngelTrax at its secure U.S. data center rather than handed to a third party. Its online software covers live view, downloads, vehicle location, health reporting, stop-arm workflows, and driver behavior. Driver behavior events arrive with video meant to support coaching, claims response, and accountability.

The company page dates the business to 2006. It reports 250,000 active systems operating worldwide. It also states $2.5M spent on research and development yearly. The same page describes a SOC 2 Type II-compliant data center for data security.

paragraphs: SilverRide runs an assisted transportation platform for older adults and people with disabilities, licensed as a Transportation Network Company in 18 states. The driver network is made up of credentialed independent contractors using their own vehicles across 35+ major metro areas.

The company works three ways: paratransit partnerships with transit agencies, contract services for PACE and healthcare organizations, and direct booking for riders and their families. For transit agencies the service is ADA-compliant paratransit at scale, including complementary service, overflow capacity, premium tiers, and same-day trips. For PACE programs and healthcare organizations the service is door-through-door, with the driver escorting riders from inside the pickup location into the destination.
SilverRide was founded in 2006 by Jeff Maltz and Susan Steiner Saal. The company reports more than one million rides every year with 95% on-time performance.

before.name: CITYROVER
before.description: AI dashcams (EDGE/PULSE) for automated pothole and road-defect detection for public works - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: CITYROVER sells smart cameras and software that governments mount in vehicles already driving their streets, so road problems get spotted without a dedicated inspection trip. The stated aim is taking over inspection work that agencies would otherwise do by hand.

Detection happens on the camera itself, which uploads what it finds to the cloud for review. Staff get notifications carrying the location and images of the issue. The camera picks out potholes, manholes, dumped garbage, transit infrastructure problems and signs. Two other families sit beside it: PULSE for pavement rating, pavement markings and survey imagery, and COMPANION, an app for inspectors and work crews.

Government inspectors are the main users, reporting maintenance and operations issues automatically. An open API and off-the-shelf connectors move the data into systems an agency already runs. The site claims hundreds of governments as customers.

paragraphs: Consat Telematics is a Swedish provider of public transportation systems, founded in 1986 and operating across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Australia, Canada, and Brazil. The wider Consat group reports offices on five continents and more than 250 employees.

The transit offering is modular, covering electromobility for electric fleet monitoring and smart charging as well as traffic control and monitoring for real-time fleet oversight and incident management. Passenger information delivers accurate, real-time updates to riders both onboard and offboard. Every part is described as multivendor and multimodal compatible, deployable in cloud, on-premise, or data centre environments. Support runs end to end, from installation and integration through maintenance and training.

The hardware and software are installed on more than 40,000 vehicles globally. Named customers include Skyss in Norway, Tide Buss in Sweden, Ventura Bus Lines in Australia, and Din Tur in Sweden. A headline on the same page announces Bonnier Capital becoming a strategic partner in Consat Telematics. The company states that it is certified as a Great Place to Work for 2024 and 2025.

before.buyer: Transit agencies and city departments of transportation — named clients include DC Department of Transportation, Madera Metro, City of Fresno, and a Transit Tech Lab partnership with MTA NYCT and LIRR.

paragraphs: Ontra Mobility sells a planning platform that transit agencies use to model travel demand and generate optimized routes and on-demand zones before committing to service changes. The platform encodes budget, fleet, service standards, and agency feedback as constraints, and builds phased rollout plans for pilots and long-term planning. Analysis tools in the platform map origin-destination trip flows, load factors by route and time period, isochrone coverage, and census data.

A second product is a white-labeled trip planner app that carries the operator's branding and ingests GTFS and GTFS-RT feeds for schedules, vehicle positions, and service alerts. Ontra also sells operations software for bus, shuttle, and paratransit services, with a monitor app for fleet visibility, a driver app, and a rider app for on-demand trips. The operations stack also includes rider and driver applications for iOS and Android plus dashboard, analysis, and admin tools.

The white-label app is aimed at transit agencies, universities and campuses, hospitals and medical centers, corporate campuses, events and conferences, and apartment complexes. Ontra Mobility partners with the City of Fresno on a Transit On-Demand Feasibility Study. Ontra was selected for Transit Tech Lab to conduct a proof of concept with agency partners including MTA NYCT and LIRR.

paragraphs: O-CITY is an automated fare collection platform for public transport operators and municipalities, and the payment technology behind it comes from BPC. The platform digitalises the payment process end-to-end, and travellers use a mobile or a payment card rather than paper tickets. Citizens and tourists can pay with smart cards, contactless Visa, MasterCard or UnionPay, mobile wallets, and QR codes.

These pages say the platform is sold to transport agencies, governments and merchants for self-service digital ticketing across their cities. For operators, account-based ticketing is described as reduced costs, improved efficiency and easier fare management. Fares can be based on route, type of transport or service, or traveller status such as student or senior.

Deployment options include on-premise, PaaS, SaaS or fully managed operations, on existing transport or merchant terminals. A case study on the platform page describes Bishkek moving away from the use of cash. Another case study describes a Ministry of Transport automating public transport fare collection.

quote.text: To empower transport operators and governments to provide an easy, secure and transparent city payment experience.

provenance.quote: Adopted by more than 130 cities worldwide, O-CITY is an innovative automated fare collection solution for public transport operators and municipalities.
O-CITY is an automated fare collection platform which has been designed with both transport operators and travellers in mind, digitalising the payment process end-to-end.
Citizens and tourists alike can choose the payment method of their choice, including smart cards, contactless Visa, MasterCard or UnionPay, mobile wallets, and QR codes.
O-CITY enables transport agencies, governments and merchants to roll out easy to use, self-service digital ticketing across their cities.
For operators, account-based ticketing means reduced costs, improved efficiency and easier fare management.
personalised fares can be based on route, type of transport or service, or traveller status (student or senior, for example).
O-CITY offers multiple models of deployment: on-premise, PaaS, SaaS or fully managed operations by O-CITY's team of experts.
As part of its drive toward digital transformation and smart city programmes, Bishkek embarked on an innovative project to move away from the use of cash.
The Ministry of Transport decided to engage in an ambitious digital transformation programme to automate public transport fare collection.

paragraphs: BusPas upgrades, connects and modernizes urban furniture, starting with bus stops. It equips that furniture with sensors and edge computing meant to improve transit, protect user privacy and enhance security. paragraphs: Aesys builds passenger information displays for intercity, regional and metropolitan rail. It also makes variable message signs carrying traffic and safety information on highways, in tunnels and in cities. At airports its flight information displays run from the runway to the baggage area. A further line covers industrial displays made to hold up in harsh environments.

Displays carrying road information are built to comply with a European standard for variable message signs. Design and production are handled internally at the Bergamo headquarters. Testing starts early, from the first stages of prototyping. Software staff have written interfaces for standard protocols such as NTCIP, DisplayML, Modbus and TLS.

The company says it has been growing since 1977. It reports over 400 employees dedicated to product excellence. Sales offices sit in Germany, Spain and the United States. Certifications listed include a quality management system under ISO 9001.

paragraphs: Samsara sells a platform to organizations that run vehicles and equipment, pitched on improving safety, lowering costs and changing how operations work. For fleets it covers live GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, fuel analytics and compliance reporting. The company presents this as one platform working across every part of an operation rather than separate tools.

Its cameras pair safety detections with video that managers can pull on demand. The company says the system watches for drowsiness, distraction, tailgating and forward collision risk. It states that these are caught in real time and trigger an in-cab alert before a manager is involved. A multicamera option adds up to four auxiliary HD feeds for visibility around the vehicle. A separate site product brings third-party cameras at facilities into a cloud dashboard for onboarding and troubleshooting.

The camera pages list transportation and logistics, field services, construction, public sector and essential services among the industries served. For school districts the company describes arm-mounted cameras that enforce school bus stop-arm compliance during pickups and drop-offs. Among its customer stories is one saying the City of El Paso recovered $1.3M in assets and reduced accidents by 29%. A site camera gateway is listed as compliant with the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.

paragraphs: Piper Networks is a rail engineering solutions provider and systems integrator working in transportation technologies. Five primary product lines cover Vital Train Positioning, Maintenance of Way (MOW) Protection, Automatic Train Protection (ATP), Grade Crossing Safety, and Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS). Those systems combine real-time location technologies including UWB, BLE, GPS-RTK, LTE, RFID, HD cameras and LiDAR.

Amtrak selected the Limits Compliance and Collision Avoidance System (LCCAS) to protect and monitor Maintenance of Way vehicles. Piper is equipping Amtrak vehicles in the Northeast corridor with LCCAS devices and delivering real-time telematics data to the dispatch system. Piper developed the technology behind the MTA countdown clocks at B Division station platforms and mezzanines. Piper and Thales were awarded a Pilot Program for an Ultra-Wideband Based Train Control System to be installed on the 7 (Flushing) Line.

The UWB train control system received a CENELEC Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL-4) Certification from independent safety assessor TÜV SÜD. Piper states that its multi-sensor system has an accuracy of less than 5cm.

before.name: Spare

paragraphs: Spare sells operations software that a public transit agency runs its service on. The modes it covers include paratransit, microtransit and fixed route, along with asset management.

In one system an agency handles scheduling and dispatch, the rider experience, fleet health, and compliance and reporting. Because paratransit trips are often contracted out, the platform pulls trips from different providers into one place. Eligibility applications and rider records are digitized, which the company says speeds up the review process. On the fixed route side, an agency can plan service, publish a GTFS feed, build schedules and run live operations together. A voice assistant answers rider calls for bookings, arrival times and common questions.

The platform is described as built to meet ADA, NTD and grant reporting requirements. It connects through open APIs, GTFS, AVL feeds and single sign-on rather than replacing what a technology team already runs. Spare puts its reach at more than 230 communities. Its fixed route page describes coordinating a large event shuttle for LA Metro.

paragraphs: TransTrack Systems writes software for public transit agencies that pulls scattered operating data into one place so performance can be watched and reported. The main application collects data from across an agency so teams can follow trends and produce the reports decisions rest on.

Much of the appeal is federal reporting: agency data is applied automatically to the required National Transit Database forms, which the company says turns most of the annual filing from weeks of work into days. A companion analytics product presents the same operating data as dashboards, reports and metrics an agency can adjust. The point of it, in the company's framing, is to replace manual spreadsheets and disconnected systems and keep the numbers behind federal funding accurate.

The firm was formed in 2002 by transit management professionals. More than twenty years on, it describes its business as helping agencies turn operating data into better decisions. Alongside the software it lists consulting work such as transit financial planning and cost analyses. The platform itself was built with transit professionals involved.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.description: iMarq mobile asset maintenance and MRO platform for transit, rail, and fleets

paragraphs: Connixt sells iMarq, a mobile-first application built for field crews, technicians and mechanics to digitize and automate data collection, paperwork, processes and workflows. The company aims it at fleets, rail, transit, manufacturing, heavy engineering and facilities.

There are native apps for iOS and Android. They run on phones and tablets, both online and offline. Crews record asset details in the organization's own forms, on their own devices, in real time. An assistant called iBot puts institutional knowledge, troubleshooting guidance and compliance support in front of frontline teams, while reporting lets users reach their data on any device and track asset status.

Public agency case studies include a transportation department whose traffic signal division used the customizable mobile app to digitize work orders and improve transparency. Another covers Metrolink, which automated the train delay reporting its conductors had been doing on paper. The company reports winning two Progressive Railroading Reader's Choice Awards for a second consecutive year. It is run by two co-founders, Satish and Prabhu, described as industry veterans, and the site cites a 4.8 rating on Capterra.

before.name: Axon Vibe
before.description: Mobility behavior platform powering operator apps: journey detection, BIBO ticketing (built the MTA app)

paragraphs: Axon Vibe sells a smartphone-based, multi-modal mobility platform to public transport operators and authorities. The idea is to match a rider's predicted travel patterns against real-time traffic on roads and rail, then offer more efficient and less polluting travel options.

Patented location tracking predicts what people are going to do next, and psychological communication interventions are used to shift their behaviour. Riders who respond are rewarded with travel fare incentives financed by green governmental funds, plus rewards provided by local merchants. The platform is also sold to enable automatic ticketing, incentivise behaviour change and optimise customer flow management. For cities, understanding why and how people travel in real time is presented as the basis for more accurate planning.

Door-to-door journey detection powers Deutsche Bahn check-in and be-out ticketing, for example in Greater Nuremberg. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority launched its official MTA app in March 2024. Founded in 2014, the company describes a team of more than 100 software engineers, data scientists, location analytics experts, psychologists and communication specialists. Its predecessor Endoxon delivered core technology for Google Maps and was acquired by Google in 2006.

paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. They capture vibration, temperature, runtime, and operational behavior, and the stated install time is 30 to 120 minutes on legacy and modern equipment. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Knaq describes the equipment it monitors as critical infrastructure across airports, transit systems, hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. For transit agencies the stated value is early identification of failures that lead to station outages and accessibility violations. Large real estate portfolios are listed as another buyer group, with tenant disruption and contractor performance named as concerns.

The about page names Sound Transit as a client that paired the platform with its own maintenance operation to reduce elevator and escalator unreported time. The platform connects to CMMS platforms and BMS through the Knaq API, so equipment data reaches systems facilities teams already run.

before.name: Miovision
before.description: Traffic data collection and smart intersection technology - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026

paragraphs: Miovision sells traffic data collection tools meant to give planners the accurate, verifiable data their mobility plans depend on. It also sells detection equipment that improves signal performance by responding to real-world road user demand, from bicycles to articulated trucks. Its Opticom line clears the path for emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.

Portable devices capture comprehensive multimodal count data including cars, trucks, pedestrians and bikes. A newer optimization product replaces manual five-year retiming cycles with iterative, objective-based optimization that the company says cuts manual effort by up to half. Engineers compare plans side-by-side, validate against industry standards, and push updates directly to field controllers without manual data re-entry.

The company says that since 2005 it has had 2,000 customers in 68 countries and 13,000 cities, with 30 billion vehicles and 1.5 billion pedestrians counted. It lists more than 300 detection customers in North America. Detroit partnered with Miovision to upgrade over 600 intersections. In San Rafael, police and fire vehicles now receive signal priority at 53 intersections.

before.name: Avail Technologies
before.description: myAvail enterprise transit management ITS and CAD/AVL for mid-size US agencies

paragraphs: Avail Technologies sells enterprise transit management software to public transit agencies. The company states that its target market is transit operators with medium-sized fleets.

The myAvail platform covers vehicle location, dispatching, workforce management, reporting, and rider communications, so a team works from one connected system rather than several tools. A single shared database moves data throughout the organization. Dispatchers see where every bus and driver is, and incidents are tracked as they occur. Business intelligence dashboards report metrics in real time, which the company frames as a way to improve efficiency, justify funding requests, and demonstrate compliance. Features can be added to the platform as an agency's needs grow, and the company says myAvail ships multiple platform updates a year.

Founded in 1999, Avail describes a family-oriented staff working hand-in-hand with transit professionals. It says it has stayed a mid-sized company by design. An announcement on the site names Rick Spangler as president and chief executive as the company continues a transition to full employee ownership.

before.name: Hayden AI
before.description: Bus-mounted AI cameras enforcing bus lanes and stops for transit agencies

paragraphs: Hayden AI mounts cameras on transit buses so cities can catch vehicles that block bus lanes and stops. The system pairs vision AI with hardware built for the vehicle and reads the street around it as the bus drives.

Automated bus lane enforcement is the flagship product, meant to clear unauthorized parking and raise bus speeds. The catalog also lists automated bike lane enforcement. Double parking gets its own product, aimed at a habit the company blames for crashes and lost time on transit routes. The platform is described as identifying objects rather than people.

Cities buy it for outcomes on bus routes, and the company frames the payoff as fewer collisions. Leadership comes from artificial intelligence, data science, transportation, and government technology. The company reports six GovTech 100 wins between 2021 and 2026.

quote.text: Illegal parking or driving in bus lanes delays entire bus routes

flagship product, Automated Bus Lane Enforcement , increases transit bus speeds, efficiency and ridership by helping cities clear unauthorized parking in bus lanes
Automated Bike Lane Enforcement Solution
Just one double parked vehicle can increase the likelihood of crashes and wreaks havoc on traffic and public transit on-time performance.
mobile perception platform is focused on identifying objects, not people

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

paragraphs: Papercast sells battery and solar powered e-paper displays for sharing digital content with the public. The displays are updated through a content management system that can carry real-time or static information. Power options include rechargeable battery for indoor use and solar for outdoor use, with mains powered also available.

The homepage lists bus stop passenger information displays, rail arrival and station wayfinding, airport wayfinding, highways and car parks, and event panels among the applications. On the product page the company describes itself as developing e-paper display solutions for public transportation systems such as bus stops and train stations. That page names public transport operators and authorities as the organisations enabled to give passengers real-time arrival and departure information.

The software platform gives transportation operators an interface to manage displays, covering monitoring and diagnostics through to content management. It can be integrated with existing transit data systems so that display content is updated remotely.

before.name: Citiri
before.description: CitiriOS owner scope management and operational readiness (ORAT) for transit, airports, and utilities

paragraphs: Citiri sells CitiriOS, a system owners use to define readiness, assign accountability, collect accepted evidence, and govern gate decisions. The company aims it at organizations launching complex infrastructure and services.

The premise is that finishing construction is not the same as being ready to operate. The discipline the company calls Owner Scope Management runs as a chain in which the owner defines what must be true to operate, evidence proves it, and gates authorize it. The output is a Ready Score along with accepted evidence and gate decisions. An agent named Opti surfaces false greens, aging blockers, and the decisions that still need an owner. People, not the software, approve every evidence and gate decision.

The company is direct about the boundary, saying CitiriOS is not a PMIS, commissioning tool, EAM/CMMS, document repository, or BI replacement. Citiri says it is helping the ATL team manage a $13B capital program that includes more than 114 distinct projects. It also describes the SFO team using CitiriOS to keep the Harvey Milk Terminal One project on track. A companion layer, OpsCenter, is listed as generally available, while an ecosystem orchestrator called Struxis is listed as limited access.

before.name: Via
before.description: On-demand transit, paratransit, and network planning software for agencies - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: Via sells software and operating services for public transportation, working with the agencies and cities that run it. The company says it works with more than 700 partners around the world, from rural counties to large transit agencies.

Its on demand microtransit is pitched for first and last mile connections and for places with little transit service. For paratransit, the system optimizes routes and taps other accessible modes when they fit. An eligibility tool automates paratransit applications, approvals, and renewals. A planning product, Remix, is for visualizing data and testing network concepts before a redesign goes live. A student transit product provides scheduling and routing software meant to get every student to school on time.

Via also runs service itself under what it calls a transportation as a service model, rather than only supplying software. Its site carries comments from riders, mayors, agency leaders, planners, and dispatchers. A newer offering, Via Intelligence, is described as giving city and agency leaders recommendations and automations to lift efficiency and service performance.

before.name: Optibus
before.description: AI scheduling, rostering, and planning platform for bus networks

paragraphs: Optibus sells an end-to-end, AI-powered platform for planning and operating more equitable, sustainable, and efficient public transportation. The site groups its buyers into authorities and cities, operators, shuttles, and consultancies.

One platform covers everything from planning and scheduling to real-time depot operations and sharing information with drivers and passengers. Planning tools let a team plan, analyze, and optimize a network to improve service quality and performance. The scheduling side creates optimal crew and vehicle schedules. Optibus Agent runs inside the platform, connected to real operational data and built around real workflows. That agent is included for all customers at no additional cost.

The company states that it is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 compliant, using advanced encryption. It connects with existing CAD/AVL, HR/payroll, and on-board hardware. For electric fleets it offers tools that account for battery range, charging infrastructure, and grid constraints.
