paragraphs: Axon sells public safety agencies a connected set of hardware and software: Axon Body 4 cameras, Axon Fleet 3 cameras, TASER 10 energy weapons and drones, unified on a real-time crime center platform with an open ecosystem of integrated partners. The company describes itself as an operating system for public safety. TASER 10, its current less-lethal weapon, can deploy up to 10 individually targeted probes without reloading when de-escalation fails.

Axon Fusus puts officer location, alerts, dispatch data, ALPR overlays and video feeds on a single live map so command, field and real-time crime center teams work from the same picture. Residents and businesses can opt in through Community Connect to share their camera video, and those cameras then appear on the Fusus map. The Axon AI Era Plan bundles current and future Axon AI products for a fixed annual cost. Among them is Draft One, which generates first-draft report narratives from audio transcripts of digital evidence and details the officer narrates. Axon Assistant, a voice assistant on the Body 4 camera, translates conversations when no human interpreter is available.

Chief Gary Berg of Campbell PD is quoted saying Fusus lets him see live location, alerts and video from body cams, drones and public safety cameras in one platform. Axon says it is on a mission to cut gun-related deaths between police and the public in half by 2033 through technology, training and trust.

paragraphs: Safety Vision designs and delivers mobile video surveillance and fleet safety systems for organizations that run vehicles. The company says it designs, builds, installs and maintains solutions for virtually any mobile video surveillance application. Hardware spans recorders, interior and exterior cameras, monitors, sensors, battery backups and portable camera kits, alongside software for managing and viewing video.

The site groups the work by industry, listing student transportation, mass transit, public safety and commercial trucking. School districts get a platform meant to increase student safety both on and off the bus, and transit fleets get equipment protecting drivers, passengers and assets. For public safety, the pages say fire, EMS and law enforcement fleets use the mobile surveillance products, and commercial vehicle customers use them to protect trucks, drivers and assets.

Software includes SafetyNET 5, a video management system the company developed, and SafeDrive AI 2, a windshield camera and recorder combining driver assistance with driver behavior monitoring. A plugin for Milestone XProtect lets on-prem and mobile video surveillance be monitored in one place. The homepage states adherence to National Defense Authorization Act requirements in procurement and membership in the AWS Partner Network.

provenance.quote: Safety Vision designs and delivers AI-powered mobile video surveillance and fleet safety solutions that help fleet managers operate safely and efficiently.
We design, build, install and maintain solutions for virtually any mobile video surveillance application.
State-of-the-art sensors. Reliable battery backups. Safety Vision has everything you need to outfit your fleet.
Safety Vision has wide-ranging expertise in every application using mobile video surveillance solutions, from public sector to private business and beyond.
Our intelligent, expandable solutions allow for a single, integrated platform to increase student safety both on and off the bus.
Whether fire, EMS or law enforcement, first responders rely on our mobile surveillance solutions to help perform their duties safely.
SafeDrive AI 2 is an intelligent windshield Camera/ DVR that integrates the functions of an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) and driver behavior monitoring into a single powerful solution.
With Safety Vision’s Milestone XProtect Plugin, you can monitor your on-prem and mobile video surveillance all in one place.

We fully adhere to the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) requirements in our procurement processes, providing our customers with reliable, compliant, and trusted mobile video surveillance solutions.

On the safety side, cameras and AI flag more than twenty kinds of event on the road. High-confidence events go straight to managers, while a safety team reviews the low-confidence ones to remove false positives. Vehicle tracking uses real-time GPS with traffic updates and weather overlays for route planning. Compliance work such as electronic logs, driver qualification, IFTA and CSA sits in the same platform. Equipment monitoring shows what share of the time an asset is in use and how long it sits dormant. Telematics from various equipment manufacturers is centralized in a single platform.

The company points to operations running from waste services to construction. It says it was named number one in fleet management across every segment. paragraphs: CSched sells scheduling services and software tools to public transit agencies, private operators, and school boards, whatever their size or mode of transportation. The company is the exclusive authorized reseller of GIRO's HASTUS software in North America.

Its scheduling and operations modules are built on the HASTUS platform. When an agency is short of schedulers, its Rent-a-Scheduler service supplies coverage from the short term to the long term. Training runs from foundational courses to advanced HASTUS workshops. Consulting work covers efficiency audits, labor negotiations, and tender bids. The firm also advises agencies adapting their scheduling practices for the shift to electric buses.

Transit agencies worldwide have relied on CSched since 2008. The site says more than 4,650 buses run every day on schedules developed with its software or services. CSched calls itself the only consulting firm fully dedicated to public transit scheduling. It operates globally with a strong presence in North America, serving agencies, school boards, and private operators. Its experts are described as bringing over 100 years of combined hands-on experience.

before.name: Swiftly
before.description: Real-time transit data: arrival predictions and on-time performance

paragraphs: Swiftly sells a cloud platform to public transit agencies for sharing real-time passenger information, running daily operations, and improving service performance. The company puts its customer count above 200 agencies. Those agencies are described as large and small, around the globe.

The platform combines GTFS schedule data with whatever real-time vehicle location feed an agency already has. It then analyzes billions of data points to say where a vehicle was, where it is, and where it will be next. Operations staff use it to make real-time adjustments for on-time performance and headway adherence. Schedulers work from actual run times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times. APIs push the same data out to rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.

Customer service teams are another audience, answering rider questions from the same information. The site carries comments from transit staff, including an operations technology lead at the MBTA in Boston. Another comes from a transportation planner at MDOT MTA in Baltimore. Jonny Simkin co-founded the company and is its chief executive. Swiftly describes itself as a transit reliability platform meant to keep public transportation a fast and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

provenance.quote: Agencies rely on Swiftly’s cloud-native platform to share real-time passenger information, manage day-to-day operations, and improve service performance.

paragraphs: Peak Transit sells fixed route transit software for agencies that need real-time vehicle tracking, transit dispatch tools, rider apps, and NTD reporting in one integrated platform. The platform covers CAD/AVL dispatch, in-vehicle operator tools, branded passenger apps, ridership data collection, ADA-compliant announcements, and real-time passenger information displays. Six tools share a unified data layer: CAD/AVL, MDTs, rider app, APC, AVAS, and digital signage.

The software is purpose-built for city transit, airport shuttles, university campuses, and hospital transportation. City transit work is described as municipal fixed route bus systems managing downtown routes, suburban connectors, and multi-jurisdictional service. Compliance items listed include ADA Section 37.167 AVAS compliance, NTD ridership reporting for FTA Sections 5307, 5311, and 5339, and SOC 2 Type II security.

Peak Transit gives a founding year of 2012 and over a decade of developing software and hardware tools for fixed route transit agencies. A customer story on the home page covers Muncie Indiana Transit System.

paragraphs: INFODEV EDI develops and installs automatic passenger and people counting systems and has worked in this industry since 1993. The counting systems cover buses, trains, trams, subways, and railway and bus stations. Infodev EDI describes years of experience implementing automatic passenger counting projects in public transit. The home page describes ridership data for transit agencies that goes beyond basic passenger counts.

The DA-Series counting sensors are stated as accurate between 97.5% and 99.5%, at door level and without a correction factor. The DA-400 is a directional sensor that can be as thin as 13.5 mm for surface or inside-panel mounting above doors. The DA-200 is built to fit narrow doors and holds a single sensor in an aluminium case.

The GW-400 is a compact onboard counting computer that works with the DA-Series sensors to form an automatic passenger counting system. Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. Systems come in two architectures, a classical one that yields historical data for analysis and reporting and an enhanced one that yields real-time data.

before.name: Applied Information
before.description: Connected-vehicle ITS and the Glance smart-city platform: signal monitoring, preemption, school beacons - exhibited at IAFC FRI 2026

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

provenance.quote: Applied Information’s Glance® platform and smart-city solutions turn intersections, school zones, and connected vehicles into a unified, real-time system
allows cities to manage all their traffic and ITS assets under one, easy-to-use web-based application.
Data includes incoming AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status, vehicle detectors and more.

before.name: Littlepay
before.description: Contactless open-loop transit payment infrastructure for 400+ providers in 30+ countries

paragraphs: Littlepay sells payments infrastructure for transit, and public transit providers and vendors of all sizes use it to accept payments in person or online and simplify ticketing for passengers.

Open APIs allow flexible configuration of its capabilities alongside existing AFC and ABT fare collection systems. A single data platform gives operators visibility of passenger behaviour across vehicles, gates, kiosks, mobile apps and web. Risk models optimised across global volumes are meant to minimise losses from fraud and uncollected payments. Advanced PAN and PAR deny lists target card flipping fraud. Multi-operator brokerage services connect operators and agencies in a region under unified customer ticketing.

The company set out in 2016 with a vision to make contactless bank card acceptance faster, cheaper, and less complex for the public transit sector. It now describes working with over 400 transport and mobility providers in over 30 countries, powering payments on local buses, city networks and national public transport systems. One published case study describes Monterey-Salinas Transit deploying a contactless transit fare payment system in May 2021, the first of its kind in California.

quote.text: Why can a retail store set up a payment system in a matter of minutes for a few hundred dollars, while transit agencies take years and spend millions of dollars to do essentially the same thing?

paragraphs: Prodata PTexcellence provides AFC platforms, EMV/contactless payment equipment, ITS, and passenger information systems for public transport. The company positions itself as one supplier across the full transport stack, with validators in the field and an AFC platform in the backend. Delivery is described as hardware plus software in a modular approach, with integration through open APIs and standards.

Field hardware covers on-board validators, gate validators, NFC/EMV readers, and secure field hardware designed for continuous transport operation. The software layer covers integrated transport systems, fleet telemetry, real-time predictions, passenger communication, displays, and operator monitoring.

The pages name public transport operators, authorities, infrastructure partners and smart cities as the buyers addressed. Listed project types run from validator rollouts to full AFC modernization. before.name: Genfare
before.description: Fareboxes, validators, TVMs, and Genfare Link cloud fare software for 400+ NA transit agencies (SPX)

paragraphs: Genfare sells fare collection systems to public transit agencies, and describes itself as a partner to transit agencies of every size across the United States and Canada for more than forty years. Its systems cover fixed route service, microtransit, paratransit, ferries, and light rail.

The company is moving its Genfare Link platform to a fully cloud-based software-as-a-service model. Transaction, ridership, and device monitoring data from fareboxes, mobile apps, e-Fare portals, and retail channels are consolidated in one central location. For riders paying with a contactless bank card or phone, existing Fast Fare fareboxes can be upgraded for open payment, or an Open Link validator can be mounted next to the farebox. The Mobile Link application and the e-Fare online ticketing system use open APIs to work with microtransit and shared ride providers.

Genfare Link is built on Amazon Web Services, with APIs linking agency platforms to each other and to riders. Alongside the hardware and software, the company sells packages for training, maintenance and repair, and technical support.

before.name: Beep
before.description: Turnkey autonomous shuttle operations for transit agencies, airports, and communities

paragraphs: Beep plans, deploys and manages autonomous shuttles for private and public communities. The services answer demand for alternative modes of transportation within communities, campuses and municipalities. Routes run inside geo-fenced areas at a controlled speed.

Deployments are built around first and last-mile trips, linking retail to residential areas, remote parking to campus amenities, and underserved communities to transit stops and stations. The service portfolio runs from upfront analysis, planning and design through turnkey operation of an autonomous mobility network. Underneath sits AutonomOS, a vehicle-agnostic platform for multi-passenger autonomous mobility services. It plans service modes from fixed route to demand-responsive variants. In-cabin monitoring built on machine learning lets remote supervisors react to a passenger safety or roadway issue.

The platform is built for public transit operators and authorities. The company reports deployments in six states and two dozen deployments overall. The purpose-built shuttles carry ADA-compliant wheelchair ramps and restraints. One announced project, ATL Spoke, is a pilot with Atlanta Beltline that the company says is in service and open to the public.

quote.text: Beep delivers the next generation of shared mobility services utilizing driverless, multi-passenger vehicles.

before.name: Cylus
before.description: CylusOne rail OT cybersecurity: threat detection for signaling, trackside, and onboard networks

paragraphs: Cylus makes cybersecurity software for railways, built to continuously monitor, detect, and protect every layer of rail operational technology. Its product, CylusOne, covers mainline, urban, and freight rail operations.

The system integrates passively into an operator's network and existing monitoring tools. It automatically discovers and classifies all assets in the operational networks. Vulnerabilities are prioritized and scored by analyzing their severity in the rail environment. Detection runs continuously using deep packet inspection and machine learning to identify and classify threats across railway and IT protocols. Coverage reaches trackside and wayside networks, train-to-ground communications, operational control and maintenance centers, and station networks.

The company says the product lets operators prove compliance with frameworks including IEC 62443-3-2, NIST 800-82, and EN TS 50701. It describes CylusOne as the first rail cybersecurity solution certified to IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Level 3. Cylus says it works with technology providers, integrators, and rail experts worldwide. For passenger rail, detection is tuned to separate expected supervision and control traffic in ERTMS environments from anomalous behavior.

quote.text: CylusOne enables teams to investigate and contain threats without disrupting service, integrates with existing SOC processes, and keeps freight rail operations at the center of decision-making.

paragraphs: INIT is a supplier of IT solutions for public transport, selling to operators around the world. Its systems cover all operational processes within a fully integrated ITS system.

Planning tools run from timetables through optimizing deployments to managing vehicles and drivers. Fare products handle smartcards, mobile tickets, ID- or account-based ticketing and Open Payment. Operations control covers monitoring the traffic situation, punctuality, disruption handling and passenger information. Transport companies can also use it for electromobility requirements and to set up a single sign-on mobility platform.

The company dates to 1983, when it started as a university spin-off. Its roots are in Karlsruhe, Germany. It reports more than 40 subsidiaries and offices around the globe. More than 1400 transport providers are described as relying on the company. Development and internal processes are stated to comply with IT security standards in accordance with DIN EN ISO/IEC 27001:2022.

before.name: IVU Traffic Technologies
before.description: IVU.suite planning, scheduling, dispatch, and ticketing for transit and rail operators

paragraphs: IVU develops integrated IT systems for public transport, and says it has done so for more than fifty years. The customers are bus and rail operators of any size, from five vehicles to fifty and from two routes to two hundred. Its product, IVU.suite, covers planning, dispatch, fleet management, ticketing, passenger information and the settlement of transport contracts.

Timetabling runs from setting up route networks to publishing services and supplying operation control and passenger information systems. Vehicle scheduling is handled by IVU.run, which supports the entire schedule planning process. Duty scheduling merges thousands of duty elements, crewing guidelines and qualifications through optimisation algorithms. For electric fleets the system weighs charging times, ranges, route lengths and depot or opportunity charging. In daily operation it monitors vehicle status, the timetable situation and the current deployment of vehicles and staff. The whole suite is also offered as a hosted service.

The company says more than 500 customers worldwide use the standard products of the suite. Named deployments include the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority. It reports as IVU Traffic Technologies AG and has published preliminary results for the first half of 2026.

before.name: Basemap
before.description: TRACC travel-time and accessibility analysis plus transport datasets for government transport agencies

paragraphs: Basemap describes itself as an expert in transport software and data for accurate travel analysis. Its main product, TRACC, analyses travel times, optimises transit routes, and identifies accessibility gaps to key destinations. Government departments, city planners, transport operators, and consultants are named as the people who rely on those products.

Alongside the software, the company produces public transport timetables, average speed, and speed limit data for government agencies. DataCutter handles data management, with extraction tailored to a specific project. An electric vehicle routing product plans routes and forecasts energy consumption using more than 12 factors. Highways Analyst covers traffic data visualisation and analysis.

The case studies list the UK Department for Transport, which has been developing and publishing journey time statistics for over 10 years. Another describes OC Transpo, the municipal transit provider in Ottawa, starting to use TRACC for route and level of service planning. paragraphs: LiveView Technologies, known as LVT, sells rapidly deployable security units configured as mobile trailers, wall mounts, or pole mounts. The company says the units are used by DOTs, oil and gas operators, law enforcement, retailers, construction firms, and housing operators. Each mobile unit runs on its own, carrying solar panels, cellular and available satellite connectivity, lighting, a loud speaker, and a configurable selection of cameras. Pole-mounted versions instead take grid power for fixed coverage where infrastructure already exists.

The software side is a cloud platform reached from a phone or desktop, with a forensic search that sorts footage by keywords such as white car or crowd formation. From a mobile device an operator can zoom in, turn on the lights, and start speaker talk downs. A companion app called SafeNow lets employees set off floodlights, strobes, and audio warnings with one swipe.

On the public side, LVT lists remote monitoring of borders, government buildings, parks, school campuses, healthcare facilities, and military sites. The Arcadia Police Department added LVT Units to its operations for surveillance and crime prevention. Prologis put more than 70 LVT Units across industrial real estate properties in multiple states. LVT has been headquartered in Utah since 2005.

before.name: Archistar
before.description: AI planning and building code assessment tools sold to councils and cities

paragraphs: Archistar sells AI plan review software to local governments, with a product called AI PreCheck that speeds building code and zoning compliance checks so permits can be issued faster. The same platform is offered to developers, architects and certifiers, who can check compliance before submitting to a municipality or council.

Submitters drag and drop design files onto the platform, which accepts PDF, CAD or BIM formats and reviews them in 2D or 3D. The software then evaluates each submission against the city's local codes and regulations. It is built on generative AI, computer vision and machine learning. Applicants receive standardized reports. For municipalities and councils with particular zoning, planning and compliance requirements, tailored and white-labeled versions are offered.

The company says Archistar was founded by Dr. Benjamin Coorey in 2010 and began life as an education portal. It grew from a university research project into a platform that could read planning rules, run feasibility tests and generate compliant designs in minutes. The site states that Archistar powers digital planning for over 30 cities and governments across Australia, Canada and the United States. Among the municipalities it names supporting are LA County, the City of Los Angeles, the City of Austin and the City of New York. Offices are listed across Los Angeles, Vancouver and Sydney.

quote.text: What once took weeks of back-and-forth can now happen in seconds.

before.source: ICMA 2025; NACo 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026; NACCHO 360 2026

paragraphs: AchieveIt sells software for moving a written plan into measurable progress. It pitches itself to public agencies and other organizations that find performance hard to measure. The idea behind it is connecting people, plans and data in one place.

A plan is structured to match whatever methodology a customer already uses, from pillars and objectives down to initiatives, KPIs and milestones. Update requests then go out on a chosen cadence, asking owners for status, percent complete, commentary and metric values that flow into dashboards and roll-up reports. A tree view shows how each item in a plan lines up with the rest. Custom dashboards can display information drawn from any plan in the organization. A multi-plan view lets a customer filter, segment and drill into progress across everything at once.

AchieveIt says strategy consultants and customer success managers work alongside each customer. Onboarding, training and hands-on help come with the move away from manual tracking. The site sorts prospects by sector so a buyer can see how the software fits their way of working. One page groups its public sector claims under a heading about proven results.

quote.text: Plans look good on paper. AchieveIt makes sure they move forward, with the tools to manage, track, and deliver results.

paragraphs: Apptegy sells a communications platform to K-12 school districts, gathering the tools and training that district staff use to reach families. The pitch to district leaders is that the school brand stays at the front of every message.

Districts get a branded website managed through a drag-and-drop editor with page permissions for contributors and analytics. A district-branded mobile app for iOS and Android carries school information and two-way messaging for families. Alerts go out by email, push notification, SMS, text-to-speech, voice call and social media from one place. Automated translation is offered for more than 100 languages, and websites are built to meet WCAG 2.1 A and AA standards.

The home page states that 5,273 districts have switched to the platform for their communications. Beyond software the company publishes SchoolCEO magazine, with guides and original research for district leaders. One study listed there was done jointly with NSPRA on the relationship between superintendents and school communicators.

before.name: Avolve Software
before.description: ProjectDox electronic plan review for building, fire, planning, and public works agencies

paragraphs: Avolve sells electronic plan review software to state and local government agencies. The product agencies implement for that work is ProjectDox. Customers quoted on the site also name a second product, DigEplan.

The software carries a review from the applicant's submission through to completion. Avolve describes the plan review as having GIS, AI and field mobility embedded. It is meant to fit whatever permitting stack an agency already runs. In a published case study, a water and sewer commission reviews about 3,500 plan submittals and 34,000 permit transactions a year. After implementing ProjectDox, that agency reported review times falling from eight weeks to two or three.

That commission serves more than 1.9 million people. Avolve says its plan review is built on insight from more than 350 government customers. Testimonials on its site come from cities and counties, including one crediting ProjectDox with improving operations across Minneapolis.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

paragraphs: Catalis sells software and payment services to government agencies. Another handles courts and land records, automating filings and widening public access to justice.

On the resident-facing side, the company offers municipalities a package covering website design, development, hosting and maintenance. before.name: Caselle
before.description: Connect fund accounting, utility billing, and payments for small and mid-size cities - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: Caselle makes government accounting, ERP, and payments software. It is right-sized, in the company's words, for small to medium local governments, cities, and districts.

Accounting, utility billing, and reporting run in one system whose modules pass data to each other. Built-in tools produce audit-ready statements and track budgets in real time. Payroll and human resources are covered as well. So are permits and code enforcement. Business licensing and tax collection sit in the same system. A further set of tools is meant for sharing information with residents and collecting feedback.

Caselle dates its commitment to community to 1978. The company says its story began with Duane Hutchings, a CPA in Spanish Fork, Utah. Working with his sons and Spanish Fork City, he developed software to improve the workflows of people in local government. In 2024 Caselle joined Govineer Solutions. A published case study describes a city choosing Caselle after an extensive RFP process. That study says McPherson, Kansas explored six different government accounting software solutions before choosing Caselle. It reports the city saved four full workdays each month after the transition.

before.name: Aurigo Software
before.description: Masterworks capital program and construction management for DOTs, cities, water, and transit - exhibited at NACE 2026

paragraphs: Aurigo Software sells capital program management software to government agencies that plan, build and maintain public infrastructure. It also serves facility owners in areas such as data centers, life sciences, manufacturing, and energy and utilities. The company's platform, Masterworks, brings planning, execution, financials, right of way and analytics together in one system.

On the delivery side it coordinates contracts, schedules, costs and field work so teams can hold to the original plan and keep a complete audit trail. Compliance, funding transparency and governance are meant to sit inside everyday work so public money stays accountable. Agencies can change forms, workflows, business rules and dashboards through configuration rather than code. An AI layer called Lumina supports decision-making with compliance and governance built in, and the company says every insight and recommendation it produces can be audited and traced.

Cities, counties, transit agencies and transportation departments across North America use the platform to manage capital programs, replace legacy systems and automate federal reimbursements. The company claims more than 300 customers and over 20 years of capital program expertise behind the product. It also says the software monitors project signals to catch cost, schedule and delivery risks before they turn critical.

paragraphs: B2Gnow sells compliance software to public agencies and the contractors on their projects, covering vendor programs, prevailing wage labor compliance and grant management. The company lists states, state DOTs, cities, counties, transit agencies, airports, education, general contractors and healthcare among the kinds of clients it names.

The vendor side is a cloud-based platform covering DBE, MBE, WBE and SBE compliance initiatives. Certification work runs from online applications through agency review to approval. For contract compliance, prime and subcontractor payments are collected, and subcontractors confirm payment directly, monthly or quarterly. Reporting draws on more than 400 standard system reports. A payroll line covers Davis-Bacon and Related Acts, the Service Contract Act, state prevailing wage laws and local living wage ordinances. Grant work runs through BlackCat, from applications to asset management and spend-down tracking.

The company says the software has been implemented at over 400 organizations. It claims one million users regularly access the system to register, prequalify, submit reports, manage grants and review bid solicitations. The site cites over 25 years of vendor program compliance experience. B2Gnow and eComply have joined together into one platform spanning vendor management and labor compliance. Hosting is described as fully redundant, with guaranteed availability of 99.9% and SOC 2 Type 2 certification.

before.name: bids&tenders
before.description: eProcurement bid management and supplier portal for Canadian and US agencies (Valsoft, 2025)

paragraphs: bids&tenders sells a digital procurement platform that centralizes procurement activities and streamlines the processes around them. Buyers create and post bids to a branded self-service portal, or send invitations to prequalified suppliers, configuring projects from a template or a custom setup. Registered suppliers, supplier questions and electronic submissions are managed in one central platform, where a compliance checker screens bids before evaluation.

Evaluation templates and online evaluations feed automatic bid analysis and a digital scorecard. Contract management covers contracts, expiry notifications, purchase orders, change orders and insurance certificates online. Reporting tracks spend, team resource loading and upcoming project tasks. Add-on modules offered to agencies include Award Approvals, Contract Builder with DocuSign, Supplier Performance, Open Data and Single Sign-On.

The Kinetic GPO announcement describes an eProcurement platform for public sector organizations across Canada and the United States. The same page states the platform is used by government agencies, municipalities, utilities, healthcare organizations, educational institutions, and engineering and construction firms across Canada and the United States. Since November 2025, bids&tenders has been part of Valsoft Corporation.

before.name: Boostlingo
before.description: Interpretation management and delivery platform (video/phone) used by courts and agencies

paragraphs: Boostlingo sells language access services along with the software to run them, helping organizations communicate across languages by combining human interpreters and AI. Interpreting, translation and multilingual events sit together on one platform.

For on-demand work a user selects a language, requests an interpreter and starts a session by phone or video without an appointment. The company states access to more than 17,000 human interpreters across over 300 languages. AI interpreting covers 23 languages and can roll over to human interpreters. Behind the sessions sits a management system for interpreter scheduling, routing, credentials, rate management, billing and reporting.

The company names healthcare systems, public agencies, schools, nonprofits, businesses and language service providers among the teams it serves. Interpreters are said to need a minimum of three years of experience. The site describes SOC 2 Type II compliance and HIPAA-compliant workflows for secure interpreting.

before.name: Bid Locker
before.description: Electronic bid submission platform plus Bid Finder opportunity search for local agencies

paragraphs: Bid Locker Inc. makes an online bid submission platform for government agencies. The company notes that many agencies post solicitations online but have no way to accept bids electronically. It describes the service as secure bid submission and e-procurement.

Vendors set up one profile and share it with every agency they would like to do business with. There is no cost to a vendor for using it. Setting up that profile takes about ten minutes. A vendor dashboard saves keyword searches and agency watchlists. Vendors can search open RFPs, ITBs and other contracting opportunities. Those searches can specify keyword tags and commodity codes. On the agency side, setting up a new solicitation for vendor bid submission takes moments. Submitted bids are then reviewed through a bid review dashboard.

Agencies from coast to coast use it to publish contracting opportunities. The agencies browsable by region include the Kentucky Community and Technical College System. Seattle Public Schools also appears on that list.

before.name: Arly
before.description: AI-embedded youth program management (enrollment, payments, safety) from nonprofit BellXcel

paragraphs: Arly is youth program management software that puts every layer of program operations in one platform. The people who buy it run programs for children, handling enrollment, pricing and payments in the same place.

Families sign up through a customized portal with one log-in, completing forms and uploading documents. Billing and account processing sit alongside, with revenue tracked in real time. Participants are grouped and staff assigned to them for attendance taking and access to health and safety information. Check-in and check-out verifies authorized pick-up contacts in real time. An assistant called Arly Compass is described as part of the platform itself.

Curriculum is sold alongside the software, one set of it created in partnership with Scholastic. A summer package runs five to six weeks of ninety-minute daily instruction in reading, writing and math. Testimonials on the site are attributed to program staff at YMCA organizations, including the YMCA of Central Virginia. Staff onboarding includes self-paced learning and support from the company's customer experience team.

before.name: Playground Guardian
before.description: Playground safety inspections plus Park Protector inspection/asset software for munis and schools

paragraphs: Playground Guardian sells onsite safety inspection of playground equipment and surfacing, checking that they meet safety standards. The company also sells Park Protector, a playground inspection and asset management application that runs on a computer or mobile device. Playground Guardian is based in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Park Protector records inspections on any device with or without cell service, and is built to CPSC Publication 325 and ASTM standards. The surface testing module captures the data fields required by ASTM F1292 and F3313, including HIC, Gmax, impact velocity, and drop height. Inspections, surface tests, issues, work orders, and complaints export to PDF or Excel.

Park Protector is offered for managing inspections across city-owned play spaces and facilities. The software page names parks, school districts, and municipal facilities across the United States. Park Protector is presented for organizations ranging from solo CPSI inspectors to large municipal departments. Organizations that already have maintenance staff managing their facilities are offered the Park Protector app.

quote.text: Park Protector replaces clipboards, spreadsheets, and disconnected tools with a single app built around how inspection professionals actually work: in the field, across dozens of locations, with or without a signal.

before.name: Athletify
before.description: Staff scheduling software built for parks and rec departments (flat annual pricing)

paragraphs: Athletify makes staff scheduling software for parks and recreation departments, pulling every program and every worker into one schedule that a manager can filter as needed. Staff need only one login even when they hold several positions.

Shifts can be filtered and grouped by program, location, position, or staff member, and the views a department reaches for most often can be saved. Requests to drop a shift, claim a shift, or take time off arrive in a centralized inbox that all admins share. Age limitation tools let a department create and enforce scheduling rules for younger workers, including restrictions that keep them off early morning or late evening shifts. Messaging is built in, with channels for different staff groups such as lifeguards or referees.

The company says it has heard from hundreds of cities about the struggle of managing staff, and it is looking for beta partners to help shape the tool. Pricing is advertised without tiers or per-user fees. The site dates the beta program as running until July 1, 2025.

before.name: MyVolunteer
before.description: Volunteer registration and tracking with integrated background screening (CRC product)

paragraphs: MyVolunteer is a volunteer management platform covering recruitment, scheduling, tracking, and reporting. Onboarding runs on customizable forms and automated processes, and the platform tracks volunteer hours and generates reports on impact and performance. Volunteers themselves get a self-service portal for managing their schedules, hours, and profiles.

In healthcare the platform is aimed at hospitals, clinics, and healthcare organizations, and handles background checks, ongoing criminal monitoring, and certification tracking. The K-12 school version manages parent volunteers, classroom aides, and event helpers, and checks that individuals meet background check requirements. Government agencies are named as a third market, with screening and volunteer tracking set against federal, state, and local regulations.

The product was developed by background screening experts and integrates with a background and criminal monitoring platform. The about page names nonprofits, schools, healthcare providers, and government agencies as the organizations the company works with.

before.name: CIMS Cemetery Software
before.description: Cemetery records and GIS mapping software plus drone/GPR services (Ramaker & Associates)

paragraphs: CIMS sells cemetery management software that keeps maps, records and finances in one place. It is used by municipal, faith-based, private, and association-managed cemeteries of all sizes across the United States and Canada.

The top tier connects interment and ownership records to GIS smart maps of the cemetery grounds. The platform is cloud-based, reachable from anywhere with an internet connection. Packages are tiered, and every tier includes core cemetery management tools. Ground penetrating radar data can be brought into any of the three tiers. Drone imagery supplies high-resolution photos for the maps. An add-on called Burial Search lets the public look up records on the web, a smartphone, or an on-site kiosk.

For cemeteries still on paper, the company moves analog or digital records into the new database. It states that more than 1,200 cemeteries have invested in CIMS. A page for Catholic customers says it helps dioceses and parishes protect burial records. Subscriptions include unlimited training and technical support at no additional charge.

paragraphs: EPIC iO sells AI-driven monitoring for physical sites, along with the wireless connectivity that keeps those locations online. Its named settings are utilities, oil and gas, construction, retail and industrial sites. Both sides run on a software platform the company calls EPIC Cortex.

The video analysis is meant to separate security events from environmental activity such as weather or wildlife, which cuts false alarms. License plate recognition adds vehicle awareness at site entrances, along the perimeter and for vehicle activity on site. For police use, the LPR page says the system alerts officers and dispatchers within seconds. On the connectivity side, the company offers primary, backup and failover links across 5G, satellite and fixed networks. The same platform centralizes SIM and device management across multiple carriers with real-time usage monitoring.

For public safety and critical infrastructure customers, EPIC iO frames its role as situational awareness that supports emergency response without replacing established response protocols. Homepage testimonials are attributed anonymously, by role, to bodies such as a municipal public safety agency. The about page names an AI platform called DeepInsights as the cornerstone of its mission.

before.name: TeamLinkt
before.description: Free team and league management platform monetized via payments and ads; $8.3M Series A 2025

paragraphs: TeamLinkt sells sports registration, scheduling, and administration software to the organizations that run seasons. Registration forms are built inside the platform and payments are collected online, and schedules are published from the same place. An app puts schedules, scores, standings, and updates in front of athletes and their families, with team chat in place of scattered texts and email chains.

League operators get tools for building balanced schedules, tracking standings, assigning officials, and running game day operations across divisions. Clubs and associations get registration templates, rostering, scheduling across fields, courts, and ice times, and tracking of waivers, background checks, and certifications. Governing bodies register and manage their member clubs and associations, track compliance across them, and can run their own competitions.

Core features are free, with a paid bundle for organizations that want more advanced tools. An account is offered with no contract and no credit card. Support is offered over live chat rather than a ticket based queue.

before.name: PlotBox
before.description: Cloud cemetery and crematory management with georectified GIS mapping for munis and funeral groups

paragraphs: PlotBox sells software for running cemeteries, crematories and funeral homes. The company pitches it as a way to centralise the key functions of a deathcare operation in one easy-to-use platform.

Mapping tools let staff visualise a cemetery layout, manage plot inventory and track burial locations. Scheduling covers cremations, burials and services across multiple locations. Finance modules handle invoicing, payments, receipts and trust fund management. A public-facing side gives families a search tool for finding the resting places of relatives.

Sean and Leona McAllister founded the company, which combines deathcare management software with georectified mapping. It reports over 130 employees globally. Case studies describe work with Calderdale Council on its bereavement services operations. Another covers Liverpool City Council and its cremation services.

paragraphs: Sol sells solar lighting systems for outdoor spaces. The EverGen Series covers streets and roadways, trails, parks, parking lots, and commercial and industrial facilities. The UP Series is an all-in-two range using a NiMH battery and an Energy Management System.

The iSSL Series is an all-in-one range combining a horizontal solar panel, an LED module, and a NiMH battery in one enclosure. The Alto is a solar-powered bollard for parks and pathways. The EverGen 3 is offered for streets, trails, parks, and commercial sites.
Buyers described on these pages range from local governments to international corporations. Funding routes listed for projects include government grants, tax credits, and subscription-based pricing.

acquired.deal: Acquired by Banyan Software on 12 June 2024, terms undisclosed; founder Bob Cote stayed on as CEO. Announced on the acquirer's own site: https://banyansoftware.com/2024/06/12/subitup. SubItUp's own site makes no mention of it.

paragraphs: SubItUp sells workforce scheduling and time-management software for shift-based teams. The platform builds staff schedules, lets employees swap and pick up shifts without manager intervention, tracks hours with a built-in time clock, and exports hours worked straight to payroll. A built-in time clock can turn any internet-enabled device into a clock-in point, and hours reconcile automatically before they reach payroll.

The pages name higher education, municipal parks and recreation, healthcare, retail and franchise, and live events among the settings the software is built for. Staff can add, drop, and swap their own shifts with peers, and a manager approves the swap once staff agree to it. Managers set the maximum hours staff can work by role and location, including across teams within one organization.
Payroll exports are built for platforms including ADP, Intuit QuickBooks, Oracle PeopleSoft, Workday, and Paychex. Pricing is based on the number of employees scheduled, with a 10-employee minimum.

quote.text: Social Scheduling™ is SubItUp's answer to the extra time managers spend trying to find coverage after employees drop a shift.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, ICMA 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

before.name: CampDoc
before.description: Camp management software with electronic health records for camps, schools, and youth programs

paragraphs: CampDoc sells camp and youth program software built for registration, health management, and day-to-day operations. The buyers are organizations that run programs for children and students, and the company says it powers more than 1,250 camps, youth programs and school programs. Signups, payments, rosters and family-facing workflows sit in one place.

On the health side, staff collect health forms, manage medications, document incidents, and keep records accessible when they need them. The health forms are digital and use conditional logic. Medication administration runs through an eMAR. Attendance, communication, reporting and daily program operations are kept together in one place. before.description: Fleet, fuel, and enterprise asset management software for governments and universities (Volaris) - exhibited at NAFA I&E 2026

paragraphs: AssetWorks builds software, hardware and consulting services for organizations whose work centers on assets and infrastructure. The buyers run commercial fleets or public infrastructure and want to control operating costs.

The fleet system, FleetFocus, is a central platform for maintenance, asset lifecycle tracking, fueling and reporting. A companion product, FuelFocus, watches fuel levels and transactions in real time so discrepancies surface immediately. A mobile extension puts inventory and work order management in the hands of technicians and storekeepers. A Power BI connection supports custom dashboards, advanced reporting and lifecycle analytics on the same data.

The company puts its own history at more than 40 years and the home page counts over 1,000 organizations using the products. Listed offices include one in Berwyn, Pennsylvania and a San Antonio location for education facilities, real estate and planning software. Case studies describe a county internal services department managing roughly 20,000 vehicles. Another covers a regional public transit agency running a fleet of more than 427 active vehicles.

before.name: Eventeny
before.description: Event management SaaS: vendor applications, ticketing, maps, and sponsors for festivals and city events

paragraphs: Eventeny sells event management software that makes it easier to manage vendors, volunteers, attendees, sponsors and maps in one place. The platform is used for festivals, conferences, expos, markets, parades and community gatherings.

Organizers build maps from scratch or on Google Maps with a drag-and-drop event mapping tool. Booths are assigned and spaces connected to tickets from that same place. Vendor and artist applications move through flexible workflows with built-in jury tools. Ticketing covers sales, upgrades and guest check-in with QR codes. Volunteer shifts can be scheduled, team leads assigned, and the crew contacted in one place. Sponsor packages can be customized to fit an event's needs.

Eventeny was started by two founders, Aly Hussaini and Nausheen Punjani. The company says its product marketplace hosts over 4,000 small business owners around the country. Its homepage says more than 2,550,000 users in five or more countries are on Eventeny. It reports over 34,000 events hosted on the platform. Case studies include the City of Suwanee, whose small event team was hosting more than 40 events a year with a primarily paper-based system.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.name: Perry Weather
before.description: Weather safety platform: WBGT heat monitoring, lightning alerts, stations and sirens for parks and athletics

paragraphs: Perry Weather sells a weather safety platform that pairs monitoring hardware at a customer site with automated alerting, so an entire staff works from the same reading of conditions. The buyers it names are schools, cities, golf clubs, and industrial firms.

Stations at the customer location measure heat stress, lightning, precipitation, wind, and air quality, refreshing every five minutes in the mobile app and dashboard. Each organization writes its own thresholds and decides who gets notified when one is crossed. Alerts can go to phones or to an outdoor siren system. Countdown timers mark the moment it is safe to resume play or work. All-clears go out automatically once the threat has passed.

Colin Perry founded the company in 2013. It reports more than 5,000 organizations nationwide as customers. It also counts over 200 million alerts sent, covering hazards from heat stress to lightning. Arthur Ventures led a $15M Series B. The stated markets run across athletics, golf, parks and recreation, energy, and airports.

paragraphs: Software Solutions, Inc. sells cloud-based ERP software for public accounting, HR, payroll, and utility billing. The VIP Suite begins with VIP Accounting, which the company calls the core of the Visual Intelligence Portfolio. Other modules listed include budgeting, accounts payable automation, payroll and human resources, employee self-service, and utility billing.

The company has served local governments and utilities since 1978. It became 100% employee-owned in 2004 through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan. The VIP platform launched in 2009. VIP Cloud, a hosted version, was introduced in 2020.

The solutions page says the software is built for the public sector and used by counties, cities, special districts, libraries, and utilities. Utility billing is offered to water districts, electric utilities, and public and private utility companies. before.name: Ankored
before.description: Safety and compliance platform: background checks, training, and certification tracking for youth sports

paragraphs: Ankored automates safety and compliance work for youth sports programs, from background checks on adults through to verification of the players themselves. The company says it brings youth and adult requirements under federal, state and governing body standards into one system.

For clubs and leagues that means automated background checks, training and verification for every coach and volunteer. On the player side it handles age and identity verification. It connects to the sport management tools an organization already runs so coach and player records sit together. Automated reminders and audit ready reports take the place of chasing paperwork.

Parks and recreation departments are one of the named audiences, with staff, volunteer and youth compliance managed across programs, sites and seasons. One case study on the site describes a parks department replacing paper forms with a digital system covering 26 recreation centers. The company's writing points to more than thirty states that now require background checks.

before.name: CommunityPass
before.description: Online registration, membership, and payments for parks & rec departments and community schools

paragraphs: CommunityPass is cloud-based software that powers schools, recreation centers, community organizations, and sports leagues. It comes from Capturepoint, whose founder the company names as Joe Oriente.

The product began in 2002 with a town Sports Council overwhelmed by hundreds of paper registration forms as athletic sign-ups climbed. The answer was a single account on one website through which families reach registration for every participating organization in town. Departments can offer registration for classes, activities, programs, and trips, with options to buy merchandise and tickets. Payments accept multiple forms with recurring billing and plans while maintaining PCI compliance.

Check-in and check-out are contactless and digital, with pick-up timestamps and real-time emergency contact information for authorized parents. Staff can choose from 300+ pre-built reports covering attendance, financial, roster, and statistical data, or build their own. The company says CommunityPass has grown to serve parks and recreation organizations and schools all across the country.

before.name: Eproval
before.description: Special event, film, and complex permit approval workflow SaaS for cities

paragraphs: Eproval sells permitting software to local government offices that handle special events and film shoots. The platform has since stretched to other complex application and approval work, including government grants and filming approvals.

Each application keeps comments, emails, activity, documents and approvals in one place. Review is coordinated across the departments that have to sign off on a permit. Pricing is one annual subscription with unlimited user licenses. Reports can be built from any data the agency collects. An extra module covers payment and invoicing.

An operations manager quoted on the case studies page says Denver's Office of Special Events gained operational efficiencies after adopting the software. The company says its team has spent more than 20 years building web applications for clients in local government, tourism and chambers of commerce. It describes itself as a SaaS company working in the eGov market. A published corporate social responsibility policy states a commitment to protecting the privacy and security of client data.

paragraphs: HopSkipDrive arranges rides for students who cannot be served by a traditional school bus route. The company calls itself a technology company that solves complex transportation challenges where there is a heightened need for safety, equity, and care.

Rides come through a marketplace connecting kids, older adults, or anyone needing extra support to highly vetted caregivers on wheels. The homepage says rides are licensed, regulated, and ready in six hours. Ride types span McKinney-Vento, foster care, special needs and IEPs, charter schools, general education, after school, and career and technical education. Districts also use RouteWise AI, which optimizes routes for buses and small vehicles.

Denver Public Schools is described on the site as using RouteWise AI to optimize its multimodal transportation system. Cypress-Fairbanks Independent School District decided to outsource its McKinney-Vento and a portion of foster transportation to the company. Counties, government agencies, and nonprofits are also named as groups the company supports. It traces its start to three working moms trying to get their busy kids to and from school and activities.

before.name: Facilitron
before.description: Facility use scheduling, rental and payments platform for school districts

paragraphs: Facilitron connects people looking for event space with the public buildings and fields that can host them. The other half is management software designed for schools, colleges and cities that own those spaces.

Its scheduling platform holds internal bookings and community requests on one calendar, so staff can manage sports practices, plays and other events in the same place. Renters find, request, insure and pay for spaces online. Requests arrive already carrying the organization's own rates, policies and approval workflows. Facilitron collects the payments, automates invoices, facilitates renter insurance and manages credits and refunds. A building automation tie-in schedules HVAC, lighting, irrigation and locks around each event. A separate mobile tool handles California's Williams Act facility inspections.

Facilities from over 15,000 K-12 schools, colleges and municipalities are listed on the marketplace. School districts, municipalities, nonprofits and businesses all use it, whether to lease space out or to find it. The company states that its services are sustained through service fees on external rental amounts rather than direct charges.

before.name: 3rd Eye
before.description: Camera and telematics systems for refuse fleets used by municipal sanitation departments

paragraphs: 3rd Eye sells modular, subscription-based software that runs on top of its own heavy-duty truck camera systems. Its buyers are waste hauling companies that have to manage collection fleets safely and stay connected to their customers. A truck can carry up to eight cameras for a full view around the vehicle.

Video and telematics data upload to the cloud, where they become safety events that a review team turns into driver coaching material. A maintenance module watches the chassis, body and equipment continuously. It hands mechanics a list of repairs ranked by severity or by how long remains before failure. Other modules take on tax paperwork, recording the data behind IFTA reporting and excise fuel tax recovery.

Contamination detection spots recycling contamination and other non-conforming refuse at the point of collection. Adding the route review module helps haulers plan and report the annual reviews that California State Bill 1383 requires. Container quality reviews photograph and geolocate each collection event to find carts needing repair or replacement. The company presents itself as part of Environmental Solutions Group alongside Soft-Pak and Heil, under the Connected Collections banner. Equipment can be taken monthly rather than bought outright, on what the company calls a Hardware as a Service model.

paragraphs: AMP designs, builds, and operates facilities that sort single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste using artificial intelligence. The buyers are waste companies and municipalities, offered sortation services and automation at scale.

The facility product, AMP ONE, is a fully automated sorting plant. It takes in single stream material, municipal solid waste, plant residue and mixed plastics and turns them into bales.
